title: Burning During Urination
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a sexually active young adult who presents with dysuria, purulent urethral discharge, and scrotal swelling. The patient admits to illicit drug use and risky sexual practices. Chlamydia trachomatis is the most common bacterial STI — an obligate intracellular pathogen. Co-infection with gonorrhea is common (40% of women, 20% of men), so empiric treatment for both is recommended even if only chlamydia is confirmed. Most cases are asymptomatic (80% women, 50% men), making the presence of overt urethritis clinically useful. First-line diagnosis is NAAT (DNA probe) on first-catch urine. Treatment: azithromycin 1g PO single dose OR doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 7 days. Sexual partners must be treated. Screen for all STIs (gonorrhea, HIV, hepatitis B/C, syphilis, HSV).

physical_exam.genitourinary: Purulent urethral discharge. Dysuria. Scrotal swelling. No CVA tenderness (rules out pyelo).

decoys.label: Ciprofloxacin / Levofloxacin alone
decoys.reason_wrong: Fluoroquinolones are NOT first-line for chlamydia. Azithromycin or doxycycline is the treatment of choice.

decoys.label: Treat without STI panel
decoys.reason_wrong: Co-infection with gonorrhea, HIV, hepatitis B/C, and syphilis is common. Full STI screening is mandatory.

teach_me_steps.order: NAAT on first-catch urine for chlamydia AND gonorrhea
teach_me_steps.reasoning: NAAT (DNA probe) is first-line for chlamydia diagnosis. Test for gonorrhea simultaneously — 20-40% co-infection rate.

teach_me_steps.order: Empiric treatment for chlamydia AND gonorrhea
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Azithromycin 1g PO once OR doxycycline 100mg BID x 7d. Empiric gonorrhea coverage recommended due to high co-infection rate.

teach_me_steps.order: Full STI screening (HIV, HBV, HCV, syphilis, HSV)
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Presence of one STI increases risk of others. Screen for all.

teach_me_steps.order: Treat sexual partners + safe sex counseling
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Partners must be treated to prevent reinfection. Review safe sex practices and substance use counseling.

case_summary: Chlamydia urethritis — most common bacterial STI. NAAT on urine confirms. Azithromycin 1g PO once. Partner treated. Full STI panel. Office management.
